indicators.note: organisation means the letters of obit chimes are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A scientist's obituary chimes with the institution they worked for.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Scientist is a link meaning 'is'. 'with organisation' looks like part of the obituary's story but signals the rearranging of OBITCHIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: A researcher studying the chemistry of living things is a kind of scientist.

definitions.meaning: first as in top, finest, number one
defeat as in beat, get the better of

explanation.surface: A team's opening loss of the season.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the superlative of good, i.e. top, and a verb for outdoing an opponent.

parts.note: fast here is going without food, not speed; its opposite is eating too much

explanation.surface: A question asking what slow means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' tempts you towards slow; it is the noun or verb for abstaining from food.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without food is fasting; gorging oneself on too much is its extreme opposite.

clue.text: The horrid ref's playing for County

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of The horrid ref's are put into play in a new order

explanation.surface: A football fan complains that a dreadful referee is playing for the County side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. The county is in England, just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the home counties, the English counties bordering London.

clue.text: 'Mother', one ace opener for Lennon work

parts.note: mater is Latin for mother, used in British slang
one is the Roman numeral I
A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: the opener for a word is its first letter, here of Lennon

explanation.surface: 'Mother' named as a John Lennon song that might open a set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother' really is a Lennon song, which makes the quotation marks look like a title. Mater (Latin for mother) is old public-school slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer's or performer's body of work is called their material.

definitions.meaning: mount as a verb: climb, ascend
plate as a thin flake, like those on a fish's skin

explanation.surface: Instructions to fix a plaque on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to climb a wall or cliff, and also one of the small bony flakes covering a fish.

indicators.note: somewhat says only part of the word unscathed is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Escaping a scrape more or less unhurt.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an informal command to go away, like shoo.

clue.text: Bill Clinton's third to imbibe a new wine

indicators.note: imbibe means drink in, so the first pieces take the next ones inside them

parts.note: a chit is a bill or note of money owed

indicators.note: third picks out the third letter of Clinton's

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton's third wife, er, glass: drinking a new wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill Clinton' reads as the president; Bill is CHIT and Clinton only gives its third letter I. CHIT plus I then takes in A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a red wine from Tuscany in Italy.

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as in tendering a resignation
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Offering the boss some compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' means a promontory, NESS, as in Loch Ness's neighbours like Dungeness, not a person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle, caring feeling towards someone is close in meaning to sympathy.

clue.text: Weapon that's carried by actor with a small part?

definitions.meaning: a long pointed weapon for thrusting or throwing

definitions.text: that's carried by actor with a small part?
definitions.meaning: an actor with a minor non-speaking role is called a carrier of this weapon

explanation.surface: A prop weapon held by a bit-part actor.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a pointed pole weapon, and a minor stage extra is dubbed its carrier.

clue.text: Ritual banishment when former partner ignored

indicators.note: ignored says the former partner's letters are left out of the longer word

parts.note: extradition is sending someone out of a country to face trial, a kind of banishment
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Being cast out once your ex is snubbed, as custom dictates.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom or ritual is something handed down and repeated by long practice.

clue.text: Certain home study experiment up to it

parts.note: in means at home
to con is to study or learn by heart
a test is an experiment or trial
able means up to it, capable

explanation.surface: Someone sure that their home experiment is within their abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond dispute is certain, impossible to challenge.

clue.text: Gas with person swearing: very unusual scene before church

indicators.note: before says the preceding pieces come ahead of the church

parts.note: an effer is slang for someone who swears, from the F-word

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of scene are put into an odd order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A gassy story: someone cursing at a very strange scene outside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizziness is the release of bubbles of gas from a liquid, so gas loosely stands for it.

clue.text: Stable and happy with little sister locked up

indicators.note: locked up says one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: content means happy, satisfied
sis is a shortened sister

explanation.surface: Someone stable and contented with their kid sister shut away.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady and unchanging behaviour is called stable or reliable.

clue.text: Tour with Bake Off possibly rash

indicators.note: off suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of Tour and Bake are scrambled

explanation.surface: A tour of The Great British Bake Off, possibly a rash idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bake Off' is a famous British TV baking contest, which hides that 'Off' is the anagram signal. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden eruption of spots on the skin is a rash.

indicators.note: regularly picks every second letter of Teens

parts.note: to sign is to give an autograph

explanation.surface: Teenagers routinely sign a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag flown to show nationality, especially on a ship, is a banner.

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting puts the court beneath the other piece
troubled means the letters of prince are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A district court backing a prince in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A police or voting district, or a bounded urban zone, is a precinct.

definitions.meaning: to put weight or accent on something

explanation.surface: Telling someone to highlight their worries.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for putting weight on something and a noun for mental strain.

clue.text: Answer extract from letter I posted

indicators.note: extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A reply quoting a letter the writer posted.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick, sharp reply or comeback is an answer.

indicators.note: active says the letters are set in motion into a new order
almost says the last letter of virus is dropped

explanation.surface: A serious virus nearly goes live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims virus to VIRU; 'active' shuffles VIRU and GOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and serious, as in grievous bodily harm, means severe.

clue.text: Strange soldiers with time for scrap

parts.note: odd means strange
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Odd soldiers who have time for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight; it is a leftover piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover remnant or odd piece is a scrap.

clue.text: Smooth pistachio nuts eaten by horse? All but the middle

indicators.note: eaten by says the nuts are swallowed inside the horse
all but the middle means the central letter of the horse word is removed

parts.note: a steed is a horse

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of pistachio are jumbled

explanation.surface: Smooth pistachio nuts are munched by a horse, except the middle bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the pistachios themselves but signals the shuffle of PISTACHIO; STEED loses its middle E to give STED.
explanation.definitionFit: Polished and worldly-wise, a person can be called smooth.

clue.text: One could make a fortune with this!

definitions.text: One could make a fortune with this!

parts.words: One could make a fortune with this!
parts.note: a fortune here is a prediction of the future told with cards, not a pile of money

explanation.surface: A get-rich-quick tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a fortune' means becoming rich; here it is fortune-telling.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune tellers lay out a pack of these picture cards to predict the future.

indicators.note: to leave says the love letter departs from the haven

parts.note: an oasis is a haven, a refuge in the desert
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Love must leave a safe haven untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: Sold in its present state, without change, is what the phrase means.

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters of seen and heard are put through their paces in a new order

explanation.surface: A singer who is both seen and heard on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: He is an English pop singer-songwriter.

indicators.note: reported says we want a word as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a bruise is an injury

explanation.surface: Plots described as damage done.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brewing is being plotted or prepared, so the verb means schemes.

indicators.note: occasionally picks every other letter of targeted

explanation.surface: Something Woody, perhaps Woody Allen, now and then picked on.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital W makes 'Woody' look like a name; it means made of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant with a woody trunk is the obvious example of something wooden.

indicators.note: about says the rules go round the film

parts.note: statutes are rules or laws
ET is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Asking about the rules for a film to be in the Oscars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; the question mark marks the Oscars as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Academy Awards are small gilded figurines, i.e. examples of the category.
